content.title: Trump replacing Pam Bondi as Attorney General, Todd Blanche to step in for now
content.text: WASHINGTON (TNND) — President Donald Trump is removing Pam Bondi as attorney general and replacing her with Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche for the time being. Pam Bondi is a Great American Patriot and a loyal friend, who faithfully served as my Attorney General over the past year. Pam did a tremendous job overseeing a massive crackdown in Crime across our Country, with Murders plummeting to their lowest level since 1900," Trump wrote on Truth Social on Thursday. Trump said Bondi will be transitioning to a "much-needed and important new job" in the private sector. He said that job will be announced in the near future. Bondi responded on X, saying that although she’s stepping down soon, she's proud of her record as Attorney General, and plans to continue supporting his administration in a new private-sector role. The posts reads as follows: "Over the next month I will be working tirelessly to transition the office of Attorney General to the amazing Todd Blanche before moving to an important private sector role I am thrilled about, and where I will continue fighting for President Trump and this Administration.Leading President Trump’s historic and highly successful efforts to make America safer and more secure has been the honor of a lifetime, and easily the most consequential first year of the Department of Justice in American history.Since February 2025, we have secured the lowest murder rate in 125 years, secured first-ever terrorism convictions against members of Antifa, shattered domestic and transnational gangs across the country, taken custody of more than 90 key cartel figures, and won 24 favorable rulings at the Supreme Court.I remain eternally grateful for the trust that President Trump placed in me to Make America Safe Again."The president confirmed that Blanche will serve as acting Attorney General for now, describing him as a "very talented and respected legal mind."Blanche reacted to the news, writing on X, "Pam Bondi led this Department with strength and conviction and I’m grateful for her leadership and friendship."Thank you to President Trump for the trust and the opportunity to serve as Acting Attorney General," Blanche said. "We will continue backing the blue, enforcing the law, and doing everything in our power to keep America safe."The president reportedly told Bondi about being replaced before his primetime address to the nation on Wednesday evening, the Daily Wire reports.Senator Minority Leader Chuck Schumer took to social media, writing, "Good riddance," in response to the news of Bondi's removal. "Pam Bondi was the wrong choice from the start," Schumer said. "But the rot at the Department of Justice begins and ends with Donald Trump. As long as his focus is on using DOJ as a tool for revenge and not law enforcement, the cover up of the Epstein files, along with the countless other problems at DOJ, will continue."While Blanche will serve as acting attorney general, many are wondering who will officially replace Bondi as AG. Trump has reportedly named other candidates to replace her, including Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin, as recently as this week, though no decisions have been announced.Sources report that Trump had become irritated with Bondi for not going after his political opponents enough.Shelby Talcott, the White House correspondent for Semafor, said that Bondi was aware that her time as Attorney General is coming to an end.News: The president has informed Pam Bondi that her time as AG is nearing an end, multiple sources tell me,” Talcott wrote on X. “Formal announcement hasn’t yet come aka all the normal caveats that he could change his mind apply; he’s been speaking with advisors on a possible replacement in recent days (as others have reported this week) and Bondi is aware of that as well.”Bondi has gotten backlash from both Democrats and Republicans over how she handled the files related to disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein.During a House Judiciary Committee hearing, California Democratic Rep. Ted Lieu accused Bondi of lying under oath about Trump’s relationship with Epstein.“There are over a thousand sex trafficking victims and you have not held a single man accountable,” he said to Bondi during the hearing. “Shame on you. If you had any decency, you would resign right after this hearing.”Bondi is still scheduled for a deposition before the House Oversight Committee on April 14. The committee is seeking her testimony on the Justice Department’s handling of the Epstein investigation.In a letter accompanying the official subpoena, Chairman Rep. James Comer, R-Ky., said Bondi’s role as Attorney General places her at the center of decisions related to the collection, review, and potential release of materials tied to the case.As Attorney General, you are directly responsible for overseeing the Department’s collection, review, and determinations regarding the release of files pursuant to the Epstein Files Transparency Act,” Comer wrote. “The Committee therefore believes that you possess valuable insight into these efforts.”Ranking Member Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., issued a statement after Bondi's firing, writing, "Pam Bondi and Donald Trump may think her firing gets her out of testifying to the Oversight Committee. They are wrong - and we look forward to hearing from her under oath.""She will not escape accountability and remains legally obligated to appear before our Committee under other," Garcia said. Garcia said House Oversight Democrats are leading investigations into Bondi and former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem. If they think we are moving on because they were fired, they are gravely mistaken."Under Bondi's DOJ, the department opened investigations into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, New York Attorney General Letitia James, former FBI Director James Comey and former CIA Director John Brennan.The prosecutions of Comey and James were thrown out by a judge who ruled that the prosecutor who brought the cases was illegally appointed. Other investigations have either been rejected by grand juries or failed to result in criminal charges. _______The Associated Press contributed to this report.
